name: Ujjaval Bhardwaj
tagline: I bridge technical complexity and user experience through detailed specifications and data analytics.

about.positioning: With a technical background in Computer Applications (BCA) and professional experience in data analytics and LLM evaluation, I bridge the gap between engineering teams and business outcomes. I specialize in writing comprehensive PRDs, defining instrumentation metrics, and designing structured feedback loops for AI/data products to ensure what we build is secure, usable, and metrics-aligned.

caseStudies.title: Accredian Connect
caseStudies.oneLiner: Eliminating WhatsApp dependency by building a structured learning community directly inside Accredian's student portal
caseStudies.subtitle: Designing a student communication dashboard that eliminates dependency on third-party chat apps
caseStudies.description: I designed a student communication dashboard to eliminate WhatsApp, Telegram, and LinkedIn dependencies for post-graduate students, creating structured in-portal communities and study spaces.
caseStudies.outcomePunch: 70% newly enrolled active in 3 months · Sub-30s resource discovery rate
caseStudies.problem: Accredian offers postgraduate programs with IIT Kanpur and IIM Lucknow. Their students are working professionals with full-time jobs on weekdays and classes on weekends. The moment they enroll, they create WhatsApp groups themselves because Accredian has nothing inside the platform. The result: resources disappear within hours, mentor visibility ends when class ends, struggling students go unidentified, and Accredian loses all community engagement data to platforms it has zero control over. The problem isn't that WhatsApp is better; it's that Accredian has nothing, and students fill that gap with whatever they already know.
caseStudies.problemUser: Working professional students who need resource accessibility and mentor support outside class hours.
caseStudies.problemData: Students immediately create external WhatsApp groups upon enrollment, leading to lost resources, end of mentor visibility post-class, and zero data visibility for Accredian.

goalMetrics.goal: Build a native communication dashboard directly integrated into the student portal that eliminates WhatsApp/Telegram dependencies and structures student-mentor interactions.

caseStudies.researchIntro: Observed that students create external WhatsApp groups within hours of enrollment. Resources become unfindable within 48 hours. Mentor visibility drops to zero outside live class hours. These three observations shaped every decision below.

research.title: Rejected Slack/Discord Integration
research.content: Both are strong tools but have zero academic context awareness. A student on Slack is just a workspace user. Integrating a third-party tool also defeats the entire point of keeping everything in one place and gives Accredian no data ownership.

research.title: Constrained AI Implementation
research.content: Limited AI to two jobs only: Smart Catch-Up summaries for students who've been offline, and auto resource tagging. A general AI assistant replaces human conversation, which is the core value this platform is built around.

research.title: Open Community vs. Cohort-Specific
research.content: Cohort-only spaces go dead on slow days and students return to WhatsApp. Cross-program activity ensures there's always energy on the platform regardless of individual cohort schedules.

research.title: Performance-Based Referral Gates
research.content: Unrestricted alumni requests cause mentor burnout and disengagement. Tying referral eligibility to academic performance protects mentor time and makes every interaction between a serious student and a willing mentor high-value.

caseStudies.solution: A communication dashboard integrated directly into the existing student portal. No separate app, no new login. Three spaces built around how working professionals actually learn.
solutionDetails: Open Community: Cross-program public space with Study Rooms that stay populated regardless of cohort schedule, keeping solo studiers engaged.
Course Community: Private cohort space with four organized tabs: Course Feed, Module Discussions, Resource Library, and Announcements.
Private Chat: Consent-based messaging request system that completely prevents unsolicited DMs.
caseStudies.prioritization: Used a strict prioritization framework to focus AI features on automation (Smart Catch-Up and auto-tagging) while keeping the core experience focused on human-to-human connection. Gated mentor access through performance-based referral criteria to avoid mentor burnout.

measurementPoints.northStar: Weekly active posting rate per student

caseStudies.role: Product Manager. I owned the entire product plan solo—from background research and problem framing to feature design, trade-off decisions, launch strategy, and designing the working live prototype.

process.title: 1. Problem Framing & Persona Analysis
process.content: Analyzed how working professionals balance weekday jobs and weekend classes, identifying how WhatsApp groups fill the gap left by the absence of an in-portal learning community.

process.title: 2. Feature Design & Space Architecture
process.content: Designed three distinct communication spaces (Open Community, Course Community, Private Chat) specifically optimized for academic context and cohort needs.

process.title: 3. Trade-off Decisions & Scoping
process.content: Made key scoping decisions such as rejecting third-party integrations (Slack/Discord) for data ownership, limiting AI to non-conversational tasks, and performance-gating mentor access.

caseStudies.outcome: Designed a comprehensive communication dashboard integrated directly into the student portal, along with a detailed product launch plan and a working live prototype.
caseStudies.learnings: The mentor participation model: one discussion prompt per week minimum works cleanly at small scale. But at 50 cohorts running simultaneously, that becomes an operational problem nobody has solved for. I'd build the mentor accountability and incentive structure in parallel with the platform itself.

caseStudies.title: Rebuilding MantraCare’s Core User Experience
caseStudies.oneLiner: Improving activation, trust, and support by solving fundamental product and UX gaps
caseStudies.subtitle: Redesigning onboarding, identity management, and checkout for a 13-app health ecosystem
caseStudies.description: I audited the 13-app MantraCare ecosystem and designed a Single Sign-On (SSO) engine, guest onboarding, active provider directories, and native payment processing to solve database lockouts and user drop-offs.
caseStudies.outcomePunch: 79% positive user sentiment · +35% target activation rate
caseStudies.problem: I downloaded MantraCare hoping to explore its integration of physical therapy and stress management. However, my excitement turned to frustration at the very first screen. I faced an intrusive login block that locked me out. Once I bypassed it, I found a completely empty expert directory, a broken support system, and a payment page that kicked me out of the app to an unvetted mobile website.
caseStudies.problemUser: Sarah the Seeker (32, Digital Marketer from Bangalore) who wants to manage physical therapy exercises alongside daily stress and find a certified therapist with transparent pricing.
caseStudies.problemData: Google Play Store reviews show critical access blockers (users charged but unable to login), operational ghosting (unresponsive support/trainers), and technical anxiety over external web transaction redirects.

goalMetrics.goal: To understand the current product and UX challenges of the MantraCare ecosystem and design a high-leverage, 20% solution that resolves 80% of its trust and activation problems.
metrics: Onboarding Activation Rate: +35% target improvement in users completing goal selection and reaching the home screen
Time-to-Value (TTV): Duration from launch to first self-care task or browsing provider profile
Checkout Success Rate: Reduction in payment funnel abandonment by replacing web redirects with native checkout
Ecosystem Retention Rate: User retention across multiple brand services using the same SSO login

caseStudies.researchIntro: Conducted a structured 2-week research plan including an app audit, Play Store review mining, cross-app integration testing, and benchmarking against Wysa. Discovered that MantraCare operates 13 separate niche apps (DiabetesMantra, PhysioMantra, etc.) with a critical database gatekeeping bug: accounts created on App #1 throw an 'already exists' error on App #2, locking users out completely due to a lack of Single Sign-On (SSO).

research.title: Secondary Research: Play Store Auditing
research.content: Analyzed over 100 recent Google Play Store reviews, identifying three main complaints: Access Blockers (charges without access), Operational Ghosting (no support replies), and Technical Anxiety (fear over unvetted external browser redirects).

research.title: Primary Research: Cross-App Lockouts
research.content: Mapped the 13 separate niche applications under the MantraCare parent brand. Tested account credentials across apps and identified that the system flags existing email records as errors rather than authenticating them, causing infinite lockout loops.

research.title: Wysa Benchmarking Analysis
research.content: Benchmarked against Wysa. Wysa uses anonymous onboarding (name/nickname only), clear data privacy disclosures with open free tools, a single unified app, and highly visible crisis helplines. MantraCare does the opposite on all four front-end trust metrics.

caseStudies.solution: A focused 20% solution addressing 80% of trust and activation problems by implementing Single Sign-On (SSO), Guest Mode / Delayed Signup, Active Directories, and Native In-App Payments.
solutionDetails: Single Sign-On (SSO) Engine: Integrates the 13 separate app databases to authenticate users seamlessly across all brand services without email lockouts.
Guest Mode / Delayed Signup: Allows users to explore self-care tools, goal selection, and provider directories before requiring registration, building immediate trust.
Live Active Provider Directory: Replaces empty states with transparent profiles displaying therapist credentials, real-time availability, and hourly pricing.
Native In-App Payments: Replaces unvetted mobile web redirects with secure, native in-app payment processing (Apple/Google Pay) to prevent checkout abandonment.
caseStudies.prioritization: Mapped feature ideas on an Importance vs. Difficulty matrix. Prioritized Single Sign-On (SSO), Native Payments, and Live Directories as high-leverage Strategic items. Scoped Guest Mode, Crisis Hotlinks, and Empty-State Placeholders as Quick Wins. Batch-processed B2B onboarding, layout bug fixes, and visual UI polish as High ROI to achieve maximum trust and activation with minimum engineering complexity.
caseStudies.measurement: Monitor onboarding activation rate (target +35%), track Time-to-Value (TTV), measure checkout success rate by tracking drop-offs, and monitor ecosystem retention rate.
caseStudies.role: Product Management Intern / UX Researcher (Self-Initiated Case Study). I led the 2-week research plan, executed Play Store review mining, identified the 13-app database identity conflict, mapped the customer journey, wireframed the new onboarding paths, and defined the technical requirements for SSO and payments.

process.title: 1. Research & Ecosystem Auditing
process.content: Mined 100+ reviews and mapped the 13-app parent brand database structure, diagnosing the root cause of the account lockout bug.

process.title: 2. User Journey & Pain Point Synthesis
process.content: Created the 'Sarah the Seeker' persona and mapped her customer journey across onboarding, exploring care, and secure checkout to isolate high-friction stages.

process.title: 3. Specifying Technical Trade-offs
process.content: Mapped features to an Importance/Difficulty matrix and authored system specifications for SSO database integration, guest entry points, and native checkout.

caseStudies.outcome: Designed a unified onboarding, active directory, and secure checkout system to resolve 80% of MantraCare's trust and activation problems, validated via testing with existing and new user cohorts.
caseStudies.learnings: Customer Centricity: PM is about removing friction, errors, and unhelpful constraints. System-First Design: UX is not just visual; PMs must design the system first and screens second. Managing PM Trade-offs: Focusing on SSO rather than immediately merging 13 apps is a pragmatic, high-impact choice.

caseStudies.title: LLM Evaluation at Soul AI: Building Feedback Systems
caseStudies.oneLiner: Designing structured feedback pipelines to systematically reduce hallucination rates in production LLMs
caseStudies.subtitle: Designing evaluation methodologies and structured feedback loops to improve LLM accuracy
caseStudies.description: I designed prompt safety rubrics and structured feedback pipelines to help engineering teams systematically align LLM outputs.
caseStudies.outcomePunch: 1,000+ annotated evaluations delivered · measurable drop in hallucination rate
caseStudies.problem: AI models deployed in consumer products frequently generate outputs that fail user expectations in tone, safety, or factual accuracy. Engineering teams lacked a structured, repeatable process to identify failure patterns and translate them into actionable training data corrections.
caseStudies.problemUser: ML engineers and dataset curators at AI companies who need clear, structured failure signal to guide fine-tuning — not raw user complaints.
caseStudies.problemData: Without structured evaluation rubrics, feedback from human reviewers was inconsistent across evaluators, making it impossible to establish reliable failure frequency baselines or prioritise training corrections.

goalMetrics.goal: Create a repeatable evaluation system that converts qualitative human feedback into structured, prioritisable engineering data — reducing review inconsistency and hallucination rate over time.
metrics: Inter-annotator agreement rate: target >85% on safety classification tasks
Taxonomy coverage: % of submitted evaluations mapped to a defined failure category (target >90%)
Hallucination rate reduction: measured across bi-weekly model evaluation snapshots

research.title: Evaluation Audit
research.content: Reviewed 200 past model responses. Found 3 recurring failure types: semantic drift (model loses the user's original intent mid-response), tone mismatch (formal vs. casual register errors), and formatting failures (markdown rendered as raw text). These became the foundation of the bug taxonomy.

research.title: Competitive Benchmarking
research.content: Studied evaluation frameworks from Anthropic's Constitutional AI paper and OpenAI's RLHF documentation. Key insight: the most effective rubrics are binary and concrete — not subjective scales. Adapted this into the Soul AI rubric design.

research.title: Red-Teaming Sessions
research.content: Conducted adversarial prompt testing to simulate edge-case user queries. Discovered where model safety policies clashed with helpfulness (e.g. over-refusal on benign medical queries). Documented these as guardrail calibration requirements.

caseStudies.solution: A 3-layer evaluation system: (1) a binary rubric for safety/helpfulness scoring, (2) a failure taxonomy for categorising errors, and (3) a structured feedback pipeline that routes tagged failures directly to dataset prioritisation queues.
solutionDetails: Binary rubric (pass/fail per dimension) instead of 1–5 scales to reduce inter-annotator variance
Failure taxonomy with 8 categories: semantic drift, tone mismatch, formatting failure, factual hallucination, over-refusal, under-refusal, context loss, safety boundary violation
Structured Google Sheets pipeline mapping each failure to: category, severity, frequency estimate, and recommended dataset action
Weekly sync cadence with ML engineers to review top-volume failure categories and reprioritise fine-tuning targets
Chose lightweight tooling (Sheets + Docs) over custom software to enable fast iteration and team adoption
caseStudies.prioritization: Used a Severity × Frequency matrix to prioritise failure categories. Hallucination and safety violations (high severity, moderate frequency) were addressed first. Tone mismatches (low severity, high frequency) were batched for a later fine-tuning cycle to avoid over-correcting.
caseStudies.measurement: I'd track inter-annotator agreement weekly (target: >85%), monitor hallucination rate across bi-weekly model snapshots, and measure taxonomy coverage per review cycle. For the next iteration, I'd propose automating failure tagging using a classifier trained on the manually labelled dataset — reducing review latency from days to hours.
caseStudies.role: AI Quality Product Partner. I co-authored prompt evaluation guidelines, stress-tested LLM response boundaries, built structured feedback loops, and translated semantic failure modes into technical data requirements.

process.title: 1. Designing the Quality Rubric System
process.content: Designed structured evaluation rubrics measuring truthfulness, helpfulness, and safety. Translated qualitative human preferences into clear, quantifiable data markers to standardize model evaluation scoring.

process.title: 2. Boundary Testing & Adversarial Scoping
process.content: Conducted boundary and adversarial prompt testing (red-teaming) to simulate edge-case user queries. Documented where model safety policies clashed with helpfulness, mapping out safety guardrail requirements.

process.title: 3. Creating the Engineering Feedback Pipeline
process.content: Developed a bug taxonomy system categorizing model errors (semantic drift, formatting failure, tone mismatch). This structured pipeline allowed developers to prioritize dataset fine-tuning cycles based on error volume.

caseStudies.outcome: Delivered 1,000+ high-quality annotated training data evaluations. The structured feedback loops and failure taxonomies directly helped developers refine training sets, leading to a measurable reduction in hallucination rates.
caseStudies.learnings: Working on AI products taught me that model safety and usability must be managed as product requirements. An mathematically sound model fails if its output lacks context or safety. PMs must act as the user's voice during dataset alignment.

bullets: Evaluated GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini outputs across quality, reasoning, and safety dimensions at scale.
Conducted side-by-side comparative analysis of multi-model outputs, writing structured justifications to surface failure patterns and quality gaps across reasoning and tool-calling scenarios.
